what: Wheaton Precious Metals does not mine. It pays miners cash up front for the right to buy a share of their future gold and silver at a fixed low price, then sells that metal at market prices. This is called streaming.
customers: Refiners and bullion markets; its counterparties are the mining companies it funds.
money: contracted gold deliveries from partner mines
moat: Contracts signed when metal prices were low, which fix its cost per ounce for the life of a mine, so rising prices flow almost entirely to profit.
risks: Profit depends on gold and silver prices
Its partner mines may produce less than expected, and it has no operational control
The shares trade at a high multiple of earnings compared with miners
A low dividend yield of under 1%
opportunities: Net margin of 64% and operating margin of 68% because it has no mining costs
Revenue grew about 80% last year as metal prices rose
Almost no debt, so cash flow can fund new streams
watch: Gold-equivalent ounces delivered and new stream agreements signed.
